title: Biased Gambler's Ruin: Ruin Probability for p ≠ 1/2

problemStatement.formal: theorem biased_gamblers_ruin (k N : ℕ) (p : ℝ) (hp : 0 < p ∧ p < 1 ∧ p ≠ 1/2) (hk : 0 < k ∧ k < N) : ruinProbability k N p = ((p/(1-p))^(N-k) - 1) / ((p/(1-p))^N - 1)
problemStatement.plain: For a biased random walk with step probability p ≠ 1/2, the probability of ruin (reaching 0 before N) starting from k is (1-(q/p)^k)/(1-(q/p)^N) where q = 1-p. This generalizes the fair-games-theorem-oq-02 result for p = 1/2.
whyMatters: The practically important case: real casino games have p < 1/2
Formula shows exponential growth in disadvantage as p decreases below 1/2
Demonstrates geometric martingale technique as complement to linear martingale

proven: fair-games-theorem-oq-02: Fair case p=1/2: ruin probability (N-k)/N (verified, 0 sorries)
Standard: (q/p)^{Sₙ} is a martingale for biased walk
open: Expected ruin time for biased walk
knownResults.goal: Prove biased ruin probability using geometric martingale (q/p)^{Sₙ} and OST

knowledge.progressSummary: Problem selected by Seeker. Geometric martingale (q/p)^{Sₙ} is the key tool, analogous to the linear martingale Sₙ used in the fair case.
insights: OST at τ: E[(q/p)^{S_τ}] = (q/p)^k, with S_τ ∈ {0,N}
For p < 1/2: q/p > 1, so ruin probability u → 1 as N → ∞ (inevitable ruin)
